transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. Um, well, what scared me enough to actually come in today is that... I just keep thinking it would be easier if I didn't wake up. And lately, sometimes when I'm driving home from the clinic, I catch myself wondering what would happen if I just didn't turn the steering wheel. It's really starting to frighten me, so I knew I needed to talk to someone.
Right now, do you want to die?

I mean... like I was just saying, I don't know if it's that I actively want to die right this second. It's more that I just keep having those heavy thoughts about how much easier it would be to just not wake up tomorrow. And those moments in the car when I think about just letting the wheel go... that's what really scares me. 

I guess part of me obviously doesn't want to, since I came in to see you today, but... the thoughts are definitely there, and they're hard to shake.
Have you had any moments where you felt you might actually act on these thoughts?

Well, like I was just saying about the drive home from the clinic... that's probably the closest I've come. I haven't actually jerked the wheel or, you know, made a real attempt. But... those moments where I think about just letting it happen, the urge feels really strong. I haven't made any other plans or tried anything else, but those split seconds in the car feel like I'm right on the edge of actually acting on it.
Before this current period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks?

Well, this current period isn't exactly new. Um... the depression has actually been hanging over me for about 11 months now. It's just that this past month is when everything shifted and started to feel completely unbearable. So, yes, it's been going on for much longer than two weeks.
Before these past 11 months began, had you ever had a separate period in your life when you felt depressed like this?

No, not really. I mean, I've had normal ups and downs, but... nothing like this. Before this started 11 months ago, I never had a time where I felt this low or stuck in it for weeks on end. This is the first time it's ever been this bad.
Did this start after a specific stressful event in your life?

No, not really. I mean, I've tried to trace it back to something, but... there wasn't any big event or tragedy that set it off. Nothing specific happened at work or at home. It just sort of started creeping in and then stayed.
For most of the past 11 months, have you felt depressed or down nearly every day?

Yes, nearly every day. Most days I just feel like... like the color has drained out of everything. Even when my house is busy and there's a lot going on around me, I still feel it. I actually end up hiding in the laundry room crying a lot, just because I can't stand the thought of anyone seeing how completely hopeless I feel.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yes. It's actually been really frightening for me. I usually love photography and spending time outside, but... I haven't even touched my camera. I don't check the bird feeders with any real interest anymore, and I just don't care what's coming up in the garden. Those things used to be how I felt like myself, and now I just have no interest in them at all.
Do your close relationships tend to swing between feeling very close and then suddenly feeling very hurt, angry, or disconnected?

No, I wouldn't say that. My relationships are pretty stable. I mean, my husband and I have been married for twenty years, and we don't really have those kinds of intense swings. I might withdraw from people when I'm feeling really down, like I mentioned with the laundry room, but it's not because I'm suddenly angry with them or feel disconnected in that way. It's just me isolating myself.
Has this depression made it hard for you to keep up with your work or your responsibilities at home?

Yes, it really has. I've actually started making mistakes at the clinic, which is... well, it's not like me at all. And I've been avoiding my friends because I'm just so afraid I'm either going to snap at them or just completely fall apart in front of them. At home, it's gotten to the point where my husband has had to take over basically everything—paying the bills, making the meals... and just keeping me safe, really, when the thoughts get too dark.
Have you been moving or speaking noticeably more slowly than usual?

No, I don't think so. I mean... I'm definitely doing a lot less overall, but when I do speak or move around, I think it's at my normal pace. My husband hasn't mentioned me talking slower or anything like that, anyway.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge much of the time?

No, I wouldn't say I feel anxious. It's not really a nervous or keyed-up feeling... I'm just so incredibly drained. I don't feel on edge, just... heavy, I guess. It's more of an exhaustion than an anxiousness.
Have you been hearing voices or feeling sure of things that other people say aren’t true?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I'm not hearing any voices, and I don't have any beliefs that others think are strange or untrue. It's really just the depression and the dark thoughts.
Have you been feeling worthless?

Yes. I do. I keep telling myself that I’m a terrible person... mostly for resenting the disruption at home. I just replay every impatient look I give or sharp comment I make, over and over. It all just feels like proof that my husband and the family would be better off without me.
Do you believe, despite what others tell you, that your family would truly be better off if you were dead?

Yes, I do. Actually, that's what scared me enough to finally come in and see you. I just keep thinking that it would be so much easier if I just didn't wake up. And... sometimes, when I'm driving home from the clinic, I catch myself looking at the road and wondering what would happen if I just didn't turn the wheel. So, yes, I really have been thinking that way.
